plan.title: Psoriasis hallmark GSEA on delivered DE table
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks which hallmark pathways change between treated (psoriasis lesional) and control; differential expression is already done and delivered as de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 cols from DESeq2, treated vs control), with the underlying raw Salmon counts (12,000 x 13) and metadata (12 x 2) also delivered. Because a ranked enrichment, not a new DE test, is what the question needs, the plan (a) runs the sample-structure QC on the delivered counts first — inherited by the enrichment but reported, and required to judge sample_01 whose library size is ~4x below the median; (b) ranks all 12,000 tested genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic and runs fgsea preranked GSEA against the MSigDB Hallmark collection (full ranked list, 15-500 gene size window, BH adjustment) — no thresholded gene list is used, because fewer than ~50 significant genes would leave an over-representation test without power; (c) resolves hallmark hits to specific pathways with follow-up fgsea passes on Reactome and WikiPathways (human), each with its release stated; (d) reports the leading-edge genes per significant set with the collection versions, rank metric, universe, sign convention, and a reproducibility record.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
